We found that the bulk's high-order properties can be precisely calculated if the surface's bulk properties are well understood. This discovery allows us to develop an alternative method for diagnosing disordered topological insulators based on a well-known model for normal-surface correspondence. We successfully diagnosed both the bulk and surface properties of a disordered topological insulator with the bulk having a Majorana edge mode and found that the surface high-order properties are very sensitive to disorder.

A comprehensive review of SUSY searches at the CMS experiment from 2011-2018 is presented. This includes an in-depth discussion of searches for simplified models, direct production of gauge mediators, compressed neutralino dark matter scenarios, and light $A$ models. Furthermore, a focus on SUSY searches involving jets, missing transverse momentum, and/or a $b$-tagged jet is given. Finally, the results are interpreted in terms of 35 distinct simplified models and various supersymmetric models, including those with the focus on second-generation partners and light two-top-hadron production.

While notable advancements have enhanced synthetic image quality through neural rendering techniques, these methods often depend on precise camera data and struggle with images having minimal lighting. To address this challenge, we developed a new approach for rendering, known as Bright Field Neural Rendering (BFR), which generates realistic images from a minimal amount of data and simulated environment lighting. By combining a new volume rendering method with a new image Hallucination technique, our approach produces high-quality real-world images in diverse environments. We demonstrate the efficacy of our approach through BFR by showcasing superior results on various datasets in the field of rendering and image reconstruction.

Observations conducted at the SOAR telescope in 2021 are listed along with
related data collected from various sources. A total of 57 entries are listed,
comprising 31 dual-channel and 21 single-channel measurements taken using
different optics on the telescope, encompassing distances of up to 28.4 meters.
Additionally, 28 separate single-channel measurements were recorded over a
range of 0.6 to 25 meters with a step size of 0.5 meters, facilitated by the D4
optic. Also detailed are 20 binary systems measured at maximum separation of
22 to 151 meters, along with 19 entries from the Hipparcos catalog, measured at
maximum separation of 10 to 210 parsecs, and 17 moving binary systems
estimated to be measured at maximum separation of 22 to 515 parsecs. Finally,
resolved systems from the Speckle Program for Archival Spectroscopy (SPAS) are
listed along with a total of 141 newly identified pairs, bringing the total
number of known pairs to 481.

We will investigate self-dual free-fermion partition functions on the moduli space of curves with a specific weight structure that satisfies the Zivković criterion. Notably, for a specific weight structure, the partition function exhibits the property of being even under a specific transformation, when the curve is mapped to its mirror image through a specific type of isomorphism in the curve's genus zero theory. This drives us to formulate a new type of chiral algebra as the sketched-out curve's celetial counterpart, which is based on the underlying idea from mirror symmetry that suggests the mirror curve's B-model properties are linked to the A-model properties of the original curve. We will extend the concept of "hue-kinematics duality" proposed by N. Passerieux and T. Pappas, to establish that this duality has applications in finding the partition functions for specific types of curves, which have previously been studied in relation to the "quasi-classical" version of the "hue-kinematics duality". Furthermore, we will use the association between the new type of chiral algebra and the new partition functions to establish the integrability of the celestial super Virasoro algebra, broadening the scope of "hue-kinematics duality" to include an even larger category of weight structures, which includes several notable cases such as the Zivković criterion and the "diagonal case" studied by Passerieux and Pappas.

To stimulate the Sun's outer atmosphere and observe radio waves from a recent piston blast event, we utilized two beams from the LOFAR telescope: one scanned the Sun with a wide field-of-view, while the other focused on a small area. By combining these beams with a "beaming lens" that concentrates the beams, we were able to create a directed radio wave pattern in the Sun's outer atmosphere. This led to the detection of enhanced radio emission and interferometric signatures that indicated the presence of moving radio waves. Moreover, we discovered that the direction of our "beaming lens" was not the only factor influencing the shape of these radio waves, as we also observed that the scattering of electrons along the light path affected its properties. As a result, we were able to derive more accurate estimates of the movement and characteristics of these radio waves. This experiment not only allows us to understand how radio waves are formed, but also how and where they are generated in the Sun's outer atmosphere.

The presence of several observed results deviating from the Standard Model is hard to explain within the framework of physics based on a single model. However, models including two Higgs doublets offer a platform to explore these discrepancies. This study delves into implications for two Higgs doublet models of a significant constraint derived from a type of particle decay and observed in another phenomenon. Specifically, it examines, with detailed statistical analysis, the compatibility of a model with two Higgs doublets with established data on certain particle interactions, taking into account multiple effects. This model, when compatible with all these interactions, presents an opportunity to explain a notable discrepancy in particle physics as well as resolve a question about the behaviour of a particular subatomic particle. However, our findings indicate that a model with two Higgs doublets is unlikely to fully resolve a discrepancy in particle physics as previously thought.

To model the random movement of vortices in 2D flow, both the averaged position and the fluctuating part of a vortex's velocity are crucial, so a multi-dimensional stochastic differential equation (SDE) is used to combine these aspects. The goal is to determine if this SDE-based approach can represent known random vortex dynamics in a precise mathematical manner. To achieve this goal, a method referred to as "characteristic method" is employed to solve a specific spatial equation that involves fluctuating forces across the vortex and utilizes it to establish a connection between the SDE and the initial equation. Consequently, it has been found that, under a particular condition regarding a vortex's shape, there is an exact relationship between the SDE and the initial equation that allows for a precise stochastic representation of the vortex's random movement, thus providing a novel mathematical framework for understanding 2D random vortex dynamics.

The theory of entanglement is complex, especially when dealing with ancilla, as described in the boson sampling model. This model involves a quantum circuit that tracks non-linear interactions between a small number of modes in a photonic system, along with a passive ancilla that stores a superposition of different photons. Analyzing this model is challenging, not only because of its non-linear nature, but also due to the complexity of extracting entanglement from the final measurement output. To overcome this difficulty, a new approach is proposed, where the quantum circuit's non-linear interactions are used to demonstrate the entanglement of the ancilla using a conventional definition. Additionally, the entanglement-expectation operator is identified, similar to previous research on two-particle interactions. Importantly, our results apply universally to all boson sampling models, both theoretical and real-world implementations, as well as multi-particle interactions.

Learning short and high-dimensional temporal sequences can be difficult due to
contamination from noise, irrelevant factors, and varying lengths. For example,
staining techniques for cells are short and variable, yet rich in information when
interpreted over time. A new approach using a graphm model for life science
measurements of temporal sequences is presented. This method utilizes expert
knowledge to direct learning from scarce, noisy, and variable-length data points
to prevent misleading signals and minimize noise. A ranking system is established
to compare graphm model performance with existing methods when applied to simulated
data and actual cell measurement images.

Reinforcement learning scenarios often involve environments that hide their state, which agents must interpret themselves to take informed actions. Utilizing a neural network as a model free agent can be quite effective, as demonstrated previously. This work offers a fresh perspective by comparing a neural network's internal state to 'beliefs', illustrating how a well-designed network consistently maintains a stable state. Consequently, this research introduces a new training method that enhances the consistency of the agent's policy by matching the network's internal state with its self-perceived state, as estimated through a self-monitoring mechanism. As an additional outcome, we discover that a network trained in this way is capable of generating a meaningful representation of the hidden state, as evidenced by its performance in multiple diverse tasks.

Current action detection methods focus primarily on the sequence of actions and rely on densely labeled data, ignoring contextual information. On the other hand, weakly-supervised approaches can utilize rich annotation data like class labels without precise bounding boxes. Our new framework combines weakly-supervised and densely-supervised methods by introducing a new model that spots key actions and incorporates contextual information from densely supervised data. This model is based on a graph convolutional network that allows the sharing of contextual information. Our experiments using the DALY dataset show that it outperforms existing action detection methods, even when used with dense data. Additionally, we developed an innovative semi-supervised variant that extends lead to semi-supervised and transferable action detection with minimal labeled bounding box data. Our model's performance in transfer experiments surpasses current standards on activity localisation benchmarks.

A key task known as Image Similarity Challenge (ISC) is part of the NeurIPS 2021 competition events. This challenge is part of multiple tracks, each with a distinct goal and dataset. The goal of the ISC is to identify the most accurate algorithm for determining image similarity, a vital aspect in content validation. We present the winning methods and outcomes for each of the three tracks in the ISC. Data driven observations about the participating submissions and their results are also recorded. The combinations of strengths found in the top performing methods are suggested as potential solutions for the task. The code to replicate these results is accessible via the following repository https://github.com/christopheruk/diffusion-shareable-nc.

Our research involves analyzing a boundary value problem for a second-order elliptic equation under a specific type of restriction. We formulate this problem in a manner that allows it to serve as a limit model for a degeneration problem of a parabolic equation. Additionally, we investigate the long-time asymptotic behavior of a stochastic process governed by a Stratonovich integral, which emanates from an initial condition and is subject to the same restriction. We discover that under certain conditions, this stochastic process can be represented as the result of perturbating a deterministic process that has undergone a long-time evolution governed by a uniformly elliptic diffusion equation. In a scenario where the boundary of the given region exhibits an undulating shape, our results lead to the conclusion that the metastable behavior of the stochastic process, as it approaches the boundary, can be accurately characterized using the properties of the relevant deterministic process.

This study focuses on the evaluation of nuclear matter in the presence of a strong magnetic field using the Local Correlation Gleichung technique. Our findings indicate that as the magnetic intensity increases, the energy of the system initially decreases and then gradually increases, ultimately resulting in a phase transition to a ferromagnetic state. Notably, our calculations show that the system exhibits an increase in its volume due to the effects of magnetic penetration, and this phenomenon plays a crucial role in the phase transition.

Balancing communication efficiency and security is a key challenge in distributed neural network training. To address this, we have developed an innovative approach called DP-REC, which combines differential privacy and REContour deconvolution techniques. These techniques enhance security and efficiency by leveraging data augmentation and minimizing communication. Specifically, DP-REC achieves efficient communication by reducing the data transfer frequency and adopting a recursive strategy. It also applies differential privacy to prevent data sharing and maintain confidentiality. Our experiments demonstrate that DP-REC effectively decreases the risk of data exposure and operates securely while scaling efficiently.

A comprehensive far-ultraviolet continuum map of the Taurus-Aquila-Xeixas complex has been created by combining the observations from Gaia DR2 and IUE. This mix of data helped develop a model that accurately accounts for interstellar radiation in the region, taking into consideration extinction levels set by dust. Analyzing the data yielded data on the diffuse interstellar band at 4640 \AA~and the relationship between UV radiation and N(H2) in the Taurus-Aquila complex. However, observations of the region by IUE were hindered by a bright star in the field of view, specifically \zeta Tauri, which dominated our data. Consequently, the final far-ultraviolet spectrum was a composite of two datasets: one generated from Gaia's photometry and another obtained from IUE with the help of a synthesized spectrum of \zeta Tauri. This composite spectrum was used to create a comprehensive spectrum of the Taurus-Aquila complex, specifically tailored for analysis of its UV radiation properties by means of the spectrum of \zeta Tauri. This template spectrum was then used to study the effects of dust on the Taurus-Aquila complex in terms of extinction and to better understand the formation of stars in the region. Furthermore, the composite spectrum was utilized to determine the overall to total gas density in the Taurus-Aquila complex, specifically the relative amounts of hydrogen, helium, hydrogen molecules, and helium ions, which are essential parameters in

Our proposed solution for the Table Retrieval task uses Graph Neural Networks to determine the best table based on a given query in a document. For further improvement, we employ a table representation embedding technique derived from the Transformer architecture. This enables us to directly apply operations on the embedded representations of tables and queries. Experimenting with various attention mechanisms associated with different transformer variants, we achieve the highest accuracy of 83.0% on the full TREC dataset. The source code is available at https://github.com/tezu/t4rl.

This research follows on from previous studies examining the characteristics of optimal decision-making trees in multi-phase games where the decision-maker has limited information. Such studies are the foundation of a theory for modeling decision-making at different levels of cognitive capability. As the previous studies were computationally demanding, they were limited to relatively simple scenarios. This current investigation expands on the earlier findings by analyzing more complex scenarios with five or more stages, and a competing player with limited information, using two distinct models of decision-making. The results of this research are the outcome of extensive computational tests and validate the hypothesis that there exists a distinct range of cognitive capabilities within which the decision-maker chooses between two strategies. Furthermore, the study identifies a distinct range of cognitive capabilities within which the decision-maker selects a specific sub-optimal strategy, and provides a specific description of these ranges for different models of decision-making. The study also highlights a crucial difference in the behavior of these models that cannot be observed in scenarios with only two stages. Specifically, the decision-maker chooses to disclose information in scenarios with only two stages, but this behavior is absent in scenarios with five or more stages.

Significant breakthroughs have been reported in utilizing AI for population counting in developing countries, particularly in the context of the Census autonomous population estimation project in Mozambique.  This research showcases a trained Udacity model achieving an RMSE of 42.02 for total population estimation, and 53.36 for child population estimation, based on individual image analysis.  The project also delves into exploring the concept of sustainability in machine learning, and examines the underlying principles of population counting to incorporate sustainability criteria.

Over the past ten years, an AMQ tree, a novel data structure facilitating rapid query times for approximate membership queries while maintaining efficient updates, has gained significant attention. We begin by clarifying a fundamental, previously unresolved question regarding its average case performance. Next, a straightforward observation reveals an unsolved problem related to its worst-case performance. Our contribution is a novel AMQ tree design, characterized by a distinctive root node separating inputs and an intact, false-positive-free underlying collection, ensuring zero false positives. We comprehensively analyze its time and storage complexities. Additionally, a practical issue concerning its element retrieval is identified, along with a proposed solution requiring only additional constant storage resources. Our proposed design addresses the long-standing worst-case performance problem while maintaining comparable performance to existing algorithms in terms of query, update, and storage requirements for approximate membership queries.

We investigate the multi-particle reaction of two identical bosons interacting with a laser field in free space. Within the scenario where one particle is initially excited, a theoretical model based on a non-perturbative approach is employed to derive an analytical formula capturing the essence of a three-body recombination process. This formula effectively consolidates the results of two individual particle reactions ($^{1}S\rightarrow ^{2}S$ and $^{2}S\rightarrow ^{3}S$) into a unified expression. It is observed that as the laser intensity increases, these two reactions initially operate in parallel before their contributions gradually converge at a particular intensity, thereby synthesizing a novel symmetry-rich $^{2}S$ state from the $^{3}S$ state through a non-perturbative process. This novel state possesses unique properties, including an exceptionally large alignment matrix element and an extremely low rotational constant. Additionally, as a laser-induced $^{1}S$ state undergoes a non-perturbative transformation from $^{2}S$ to $^{3}S$, an ultra-low intensity of $I_{c}\simeq 1.6\times 10^{15}\;{\rm W\cdot cm}^{-2}$ is required for high-field limit $^{3}S$ state production. This is in stark contrast to the typical high-intensity ionization process. As our study explores the interplay of non-perturbative and high

This study introduces a multi-scale SPH method that combines the action of two different transport schemes with varying resolution levels of initial and target mesh densities, thereby reducing mixing between the two flows and meeting the Chorin-Temam principle. In contrast to conventional SPH methods, which employ a single fluid configuration, this approach incorporates two distinct models with contrasting initial mesh densities, thereby simplifying the mesh optimization process and reducing the computational burden. A thorough investigation is conducted to determine the optimal density ratio of the high and low resolution flows. Ultimately, a density ratio of 3.5 is selected and implemented in multi-domain simulations across multiple scenarios, showcasing the efficiency of the proposed framework on flow-structure interactions and multi-component interaction cases. Notably, this multi-scale SPH method significantly minimizes the mixing of the two flows, thus enhancing simulation accuracy and performance with reduced computational requirements and the need for mesh optimization.

We explore the potential of superconducting quantum processors as a means to accelerate the process of machine learning, particularly in areas where existing methods struggle to find relevant patterns in large datasets. By leveraging their unique properties, such as the ability to perform many operations simultaneously and maintain a coherent state, these processors can be utilized for tasks that are difficult or computationally expensive on traditional computers. In this study, we examine the application of quantum neural networks, a platform that allows both unsupervised and supervised learning, using the superconducting platform. We identify both the advantages that the platform offers and the challenges that need to be addressed in order to realize its full potential, and provide an overview of the first successful implementations of quantum neural networks. By doing so, we establish a connection between the growing field of emerging computing architectures and the traditional approach to machine learning.

A recent application of diffusion models in speech synthesis has yielded speech samples of superior quality, yet the method's complexity restricts its use for large-scale speech generation projects due to its computationally demanding nature. The FastPitch model, now further optimized with a timbre preservation technique called Timbre-Preserving Augmentation (TPA), is used in this study to address this issue. TPA, developed using an iterative process, determines the most suitable pitch for each sound element within a speech sequence to facilitate more precise control over pitch during speech synthesis. The effectiveness of TPA was assessed through a mean opinion score (MOS) rating, and the model's performance was measured before and after TPA insertion. The results show TPA's contribution to a notable improvement in speech quality, with a high degree of consistency. Furthermore, an analysis of the model's sensitivity to TPA levels was conducted and the study also explores a method to divide the input speech into smaller elements and distribute them among multiple models, ultimately enhancing the performance of each individual model.

This work addresses the task of spatiotemporal detection, which involves locating objects of various sizes at specific times and locations. Most existing approaches tackle this challenge using anchor-based methods, which assign potential objects to specific locations. However, these methods have the disadvantage of having a high anchor density, especially for smaller objects, and require calculating unnecessary predictions for large objects. Furthermore, they typically rely on single-frame information, neglecting the potential of improving accuracy with additional frames. To address these limitations, we present Hopper, a multi-hop transformer network that uses a novel, efficient anchor assignment strategy to pinpoint object locations. By incorporating contextual information from multiple temporal frames, Hopper's accuracy is enhanced. We conduct experiments on the NuScenes dataset, demonstrating that Hopper outperforms existing approaches in spatiotemporal detection. With Hopper, we achieve accuracy improvements of 19.5% for small objects and 6.1% for large objects, while maintaining a similar speed as top-performing methods. Additionally, we evaluate Hopper's multi-hop agility by testing it on various numbers of involved frames. With Hopper's focus on efficiency, it can easily be deployed on edge devices, such as GPUs and TD-SoCs.

This paper presents theoretical predictions for the production of same-flavour lepton pairs alongside $b\bar{b}$ particles through contact interactions or in the framework of sequential or colour-triplet leptons within the mass range of these lepton pairs. These predictions are derived at the leading order of QCD for both the inclusive production of these lepton pairs and their production within the mass specified ranges, and are quantified via the ratios of their absolute cross-sections to the $pp\to W\nu b\bar{b}$ process. Additionally, the impact of the W boson mass on the ratios is examined, and an alternative analysis method is proposed that utilises the W boson mass to constrain the parameters of the respective models. Under the assumption that the ratios are measured with a high level of accuracy, the models' parameters can be determined with correspondingly high precision. With the assumption that the ratios are known with a precision of 5%, the parameter $M_\lambda$ in the contact interaction model can be determined with a precision of 0.6 GeV, the parameter $\lambda$ can be determined with a precision of 0.0006, and the parameters of the sequential and colour-triplet leptons, specifically $M_Lept$ and $M_\Psi$, can be determined with a precision of 0.1 GeV.

Remote-controlled telepresence robots have gained attention in various applications, due to their ability to provide an immersive experience combining visual and haptic feedback. Evaluating the Quality of Experience (QoE) of remote interaction is crucial to identify factors causing distress and informing design improvements. This study focuses on the QoE of navigating telepresence robots via video-aided remote control through a realistic virtual interface. A total of 28 participants remotely controlled a robot in a controlled environment with different factors, including noise, robotic appearance, and communication latency. QoE was assessed through subjective user feedback and a measurement of the driver's electroencephalogram (EEG), specifically the event-related potential (P300) induced by the user's level of satisfaction. Experiment results show that decreasing the quality of the connection or increasing latency causes significant QoE deterioration and induces a mentally disturbing experience for the remote driver.

In educational data analysis, incorporating various explanatory factors is vital to grasp the learning process's complexity. Modelling the effects of these factors directly can be challenging due to their inherent interconnection with other factors, covariability and group effects. A suitable methodology to address these issues is the use of Bayesian hierarchical linear models. This paper provides a comprehensive overview of these models, focusing on their Bayesian hierarchical structure, posterior estimation methods and the computational efficiency of numerical implementation via Stan. Two educational datasets are used to demonstrate the efficacy of BLHLMs in practical settings, including their ability to handle non-normal outcomes and mixed response variable types.

The game of Mafia, also known as Werewolf or Assasins, is a popular game enjoyed worldwide, involving direct play or through online streaming with well-known platforms like Twitch and YouTube. Two conflicting teams, the Mafia and Citizens, coexist in a village where one night leads to chaos as mafia members engage in murder and deception. The game relies on player interaction, with a combination of risk and strategy required for survival. This study aims to outline a mathematical representation of the game's rules and initial observations on its principles and probability. Its initial application is planned in an independent research project involving a game trial, focusing on the numerical distribution of game duration and the likelihood of a mafia victory.

In a disk with abundant gas, it's not well understood how the masses of forming giant planets are influenced by the number available for accretion, especially when multiple planets form at the same time. To investigate this, a simulation of a binary giant planet system forming in a disk was run, with the planets starting at 1 Jupiter mass each and the simulator allowing for gas accretion. It was discovered that both planets ended up with masses between 4 and 6 times that of Jupiter and the simulation reproduced observed spacings between similar planets. When one planet was allowed to overcome the disk's pressure barrier while the other couldn't, the weaker planet ended up less massive and more irregular in shape. A separate set of simulations without the disk's viscous torque constraint showed that in some cases, planets could end up in the observed close spacings through gas accretion, however this process rarely took more than 10,000 years, which is less than the typical lifetime of a planetary embryo disk. Finally, it was discovered that radial mass transfer due to the simulated planets was less than what's estimated in theories proposing that this process helps planets escape their orbits, however the simulated planets did manage to send significant amounts of material towards their orbits' inner boundaries.

The electrical conductivity of a single-wall carbon nanotube film consisting of randomly aligned nanotubes was investigated through temperature-dependent measurements of variable-frequency resistance. The intrinsic single-wall carbon nanotube film, grown using chemical vapor deposition, exhibited a nearly straight log-log curve when comparing conductance to frequency, indicating a power law with an exponent of 0.5, which did not change with temperature. Furthermore, the conductance showed a temperature-dependent variation following a relationship described by the variable-range hopping model across four distinct regions. However, at the highest frequencies in the measured regime, the variable-range hopping model's applicability declined, and the conductance displayed temperature-independent behavior, aligning more closely with intertube electronic conduction. Moreover, when focusing on the intratube variable-range hopping regime, empirical relationships were identified that correlated the conductance, temperature, and tube diameter, which revealed significantly elevated conductance compared to armored single-wall carbon nanotubes.

This research develops a novel entropy-based feature weighting approach for the fuzzy k-means algorithm and presents numerical experiments using synthetic and real-world datasets. The objective is to enable the fuzzy k-means algorithm to handle high-dimensional data without needing dimensionality reduction. Several issues with the standard fuzzy k-means method make it challenging to apply this approach to high-dimensional data: the risk of features with high entropy but no cluster significance dominating cluster formation; inconsistent feature contributions leading to irregular cluster borders; and potentially leaving behind remote data points. To resolve these problems, a variable feature weighting strategy is developed to identify the most informative features and assign weights to less informative features, using fuzzy entropy and a weight determination mechanism to determine optimal weights. The performance of this entropy-based fuzzy k-means method is evaluated using datasets with varying dimensions, and compared against standard fuzzy k-means and several alternative algorithms. Furthermore, the approach is applied to real-world datasets to assess its performance.

This paper addresses limitations in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, a framework with known issues including non-convex optimization and unreliable exact recovery algorithms. To address these problems, the authors develop a new algorithm, Cluster-of-Experts (Coe), which outperforms previous approaches. In particular, Coe achieves consistent cluster recovery with any fixed MoE model, even in under-determined systems, and has efficient computational complexity. Moreover, the authors show that their algorithm is applicable to a range of non-parametric MoE models, including a Bayesian variant of MoE. Notably, the proposed algorithm overlooks the problem of identifying the best expert assignment, which is a known optimization challenge. However, the authors formulate a related problem, called colored matrix matching (CMM), and present an algorithm for solving it, which can serve as a pre-processing step for other applications.

This set of notes offers a standalone overview of the theory of chip-firing games on metric graphs along with the theory of Jacobians and Prym varieties, inspired by the 2019 Cambridge summer school on combinatorial methods in algebraic geometry.

We examine the possibility of global symmetry breaking in quantum gravity at a fundamental level. If global symmetries are left unbroken before quantization or don't undergo a phase transition when matter loads are considered, it would result in a globally symmetric, vacuum state of quantum fields. Since global symmetries are preserved in classical gravity without a material source, we investigate whether ambient matter could induce symmetry breaking through space double-notation curvature effects. Specifically, we analyze the Ricci curvature contribution and its impact on the cosmic background, referencing measurements of double refractive index from the CMB. Our findings suggest that global symmetries might remain intact in quantum gravitational states, while presenting a case for spontaneous symmetry breaking via curvature effects.

Our research presents new findings based on far ultraviolet (FUV) observations of the globular cluster NGC 4147 obtained with three specific filters onboard the AstroSat satellite. These findings were further confirmed by cross-checking the source's cluster membership using Gaia data and proper motions. Our FUV-optical analyses allowed us to identify the source of the FUV emission and its variation with wavelength. Additionally, we compared our FUV observations with those previously recorded in the UVIT GTO catalog, which were observed over 500 days prior to our study. While a blue horizontal branch star was the primary contributor to the FUV emission, certain hot subdwarfs and a blue straggler also emitted UV radiation. In contrast, we could not verify any UV radiation from a blue straggler star after applying a proper photometry filter. Furthermore, by examining the uvw values, we were able to map the distribution of the hot subdwarfs within the cluster. Lastly, our study further examined the properties of the blue straggler candidates.

During the 2016 New Orleans Sandboxes workshop, Nathan Fidler and Semyon Khlebnikov created the concept of the fragile principle, which was influenced by Baker-Gwinn's and Weinberger-Zaltman's work. The principle states that an equivariant homology or cohomology problem that has a simple solution in noncompact cases with moderate growth must have an easy explanation, such as a standard topological relation, for both compact and noncompact cases. This paper applies the fragile principle to the Mod 2 Mumford Conjecture, a hypothesis based on the Serre spectral sequence for spaces with 2-fold covers. The conjecture being false would imply the existence of Mod 2 complete rational topological complex manifolds that cannot be decomposed into connected components. The authors also explored the possibility of generalizing the principle for various types of topological structures.

The transferable relationship between two datasets has been extensively studied.
A substantial part of the research concentration on the impact of the teacher's
dataset on the student. Meanwhile, the influence of the student's dataset and
the interaction between the two datasets are less prioritized. In this paper,
we reexamine the two-agreement conditions of transferability, one focusing
on the teacher's dataset and the other on the student's dataset. We introduce
a new assessment, the interaction agreement, which evaluates the transferability
based on the interaction between the teacher and the student datasets. This
newly proposed assessment is more flexible and practical. Experiment results
involving multiple datasets and several recent state-of-the-art image classification
models show that the interaction agreement conditions enhance the explanation
of transferability beyond the original two agreements.

In our study on social network behavior, we carried out an experiment with 1,673 participants who manually distributed information on a online network. The experimental setup allowed us to accurately track how ideas spread across the network in a controlled manner. The accumulated knowledge from this experiment enabled us to simulate information diffusion in a large network and reveal its connection to the network's structural characteristics. Furthermore, using the derived rules of information spread, we investigated its implications on cumulative distribution functions and tail behavior. Ultimately, we found that the efficiency of idea transmission significantly correlates with network modularity.

Under specific conditions where the singularities of a given manifold are known to be non-degenerate, a unique mathematical object, called the fine Green current, can be constructed. This occurs when certain algebraic conditions relating to the manifold's singularities are satisfied. Building upon earlier work by Thomas and Yau, researchers have shown that the fine Green current possesses certain distinctive characteristics that help to identify its uniqueness. By applying a quantitative analysis, they have established a reliable criterion for demonstrating the uniqueness of the fine Green current on a specific type of manifold known as a log Calabi-Yau variety. This analysis involves scaling factors that provide quantitative validation of the uniqueness, as well as residual terms that contribute to a broader understanding of the problem.

The reliability of a security protocol heavily depends on the accuracy of time measurements, which are typically achieved using distance-side time synchronization based on regular perturbation models. These models provide a useful framework, but calculating their time discrepancy can be complex. For simple links, we found that the time inaccuracies in a regular perturbation model can be effectively analyzed using a straightforward method. This method reveals that the timing errors of simple links increase quadratically with the link's length, specifically at a rate of sixteen dBm per meter. Additionally, we observed that the timing errors of such links are correlated with the thermal noise and rely on the transmission power. Therefore, we suggest using a distance-based power correction formula to complement regular perturbation models.

Modern Android apps are susceptible to various security threats resulting from malicious code embedded in the form of apps or malware. Over recent years, the Evasion Attack issue has gained more prominence as it enables malware to avoid being detected by security systems and bypass Google Play's review process. This problem can be categorized into sub-types, such as evasion attacks against anti-virus software and Evasion Attacks against sandbox environments. This research review aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of Evasion Attacks by presenting the most recent developments in the field. Specifically, it will investigate how these attacks impact Android systems, highlight the most critical categories, and evaluate the most effective methods for mitigating and prevent these attacks. A comparative analysis of evasion attack categories and countermeasures will be presented, accompanied by an overview of promising directions for future research.

Containerization has revolutionized application deployment, and we're taking it a step further with Ozy, a revolutionary new concept. Ozy reimagines the container as a dynamic, schedule-driven orchestrator, seamlessly managing workloads across multiple hardware platforms by continuously adapting resource allocation based on real-time performance monitoring. Unlike traditional systems, Ozy independently optimizes every container's configuration, freeing it from rigid infrastructural constraints. Our extensive testing across various workloads has consistently yielded improved throughput and energy efficiency, and Ozy's innovative performance profiling and intelligent migration strategies provide unparalleled flexibility.

Recent experimental observations supporting the reentrant construction of the 5/2 condensate as a composite fermion metal have sparked a new debate about the nature of the ground state at moderate Landau-level-mixing intensity. To contribute to this discussion, we have carried out a systematic study using a previously developed method to calculate the trial state that minimizes the cumulative energy of the constrained harmonic Hamiltonian in the lower Landau levels. We found that at low Landau-level-mixing strengths, the form of the reentrant construction consistent with the gapped nature of the 5/2 quantum Hall phase is inherently stable. However, at moderate mixing, an alternative reentrant structure emerges, which self-consistently matches the energy of the local-density-minimum wave state and exhibits a more substantial energy gap compared to the metalized composite-fermion state. Moreover, at a relatively high Landau-level-mixing intensity, an unexpected energy-minimum wave state is discovered, which features a full gapped structure consistent with the reentrant construction and a significantly increased energy gap compared to the metalized and gapped phases. We visually present the numerical results for various Landau-level-mixing intensities and compare them with metalized, gapped, and reentrant gapped phases, along with an estimate of the phase transition separation.

Our analysis reveals that the Thakurta solution, previously considered a candidate for forming primordial black holes, cannot represent black holes with the typical properties we observe.  Since this solution is proposed as a potential explanation for dark matter, we investigated whether the LIGO-Virgo collaboration's constraints on primordial black holes could be relaxed for black holes described by the Thakurta metric. However, our examination shows that the expectations for these black holes remain consistent with the experimental limitations reported by the collaboration.

The formation of planets through pebble accretion is intricately linked to the evolution of a protoplanetary disk's density and velocity patterns. Our analytical examination explores how a disk's internal dynamics influence this process, focusing on how a forming planet's growth is affected by the transfer of angular momentum to surrounding rings of pebbles. As a planet grows, its gravitational influence expands beyond its vicinity, ultimately shaping the entire disk section where pebbles are accumulating. For every given mass of the forming planet, the density of pebbles is adjusted, reflecting a changed environment. Our analysis reveals that an off-centre planet situated close to its star tends to accumulate pebbles more efficiently than an on-centre planet, given equal masses. Moreover, an off-centre planet sitting at a farther distance from its star is better equipped to capture pebbles than an on-centre planet, suggesting a greater success rate for planets developing in disks with irregular density imbalances. Finally, an off-centre planet situated at an intermediate distance from its star achieves pebble accretion more easily than an on-centre planet, given equal masses. These findings emphasize the importance of considering a protoplanetary disk's intricate structure and irregular density fluctuations in understanding the formation of planets.

In recent times, research into machine learning and neural networks often focuses on the statistical implications of overparameterization, yet this approach overlooks another critical aspect - the computational limitations of the learning process itself. By examining the effects of overparameterization from a computational perspective, this study reveals that neural networks with higher model complexity may require (and ultimately need) larger training datasets than their simpler counterparts, thereby alleviating the apparent discrepancy between rigorous statistical predictions and the observed success of overparameterized neural networks. Furthermore, this research offers computational analogues of established statistical estimates, including a deep dive into the computational requirements for learning in neural networks, ultimately showing that incorporating computational constraints can accurately predict the behavior of overparameterized neural networks across various training datasets and model complexities.

Three results were obtained. Firstly, any Bohr set, defined as a set derived from certain complex exponential equations with rational coefficients, exhibits measure zero. Additionally, any such Bohr set can be fully represented using a subset of measures defined over a specific type of abelian group. Finally, it has been found that no further reduction is possible, with the exception of possibly replacing the group with an equivalently structured system called a direct system. These outcomes build upon and expand previous work by the author, particularly focusing on the application of measure-theoretic approaches to the study of additive number theory.

This study addresses the dial-a-ride problem within large urban settings where residents make bookings for trips between any pair of locations within a city, with a focus on serving those requests efficiently. A first attempt to tackle this issue involves formulating it as a mixed-integer linear programming problem using a standard assignment and routing structure, but it turns out this initial formulation has limitations with exponential cutting-plane additions needed for each request. An alternative and more effective approach is to transform the problem using multicommodity flow and configuration variables, but this still leaves hundreds of cutting planes with exponential complexity to handle. An innovative solution is proposed to tackle this issue by first identifying and incorporating key cutting planes that eliminate solution infeasibilities without the need for additional constraints, resulting in a much simplified and more efficient problem solution process. The method is demonstrated to provide good results for small instances, even with a simple single-threaded implementation, by significantly reducing the number of cutting planes required and speedily converging to problem optimality.

The vast data volumes generated by e-commerce platforms during customer interactions are transforming the meaning of "understanding customers." To base decisions on these interactions, it's now necessary to train models that can analyze multiple modalities, consisting of various types of data (text, images, graphics) and accompanying meta information (time stamps, product IDs, etc.). We propose a novel multi-modal pretraining approach called Knowledge Understood that utilizes labeled datasets to create coherent knowledge graphs filling in the gaps of the underlying taxonomy. This allows us to enrich the input data of vision and language models with consistent, interlinked information, thereby boosting their performance in tasks such as visual retrieval and question answering, as well as improving their ability to operate in novel scenarios by evaluating them on partially visible knowledge nodes.

Early detection of Alzheimer's disease progression is crucial, but difficult to achieve, given its slow and variable progression, where brain changes often appear years or even decades before symptoms appear, making it challenging to identify reliable antecedent biomarkers. This issue was addressed by creating the Alzheimer's Disease Progression Model (ADPM), a novel approach designed to track and forecast the progression of Alzheimer's disease based on the similarity between the patient and a generalized model representation. This approach leverages Deep InfoMax to create an representation of the disease progression that captures its essential features. Our experiments involved generating an ADPM from a mixture of healthy and Alzheimer's disease brain scans from the ADNI database and using it to simulate how the model changes over time. Our results show that the ADPM can accurately reconstruct the disease progression and predict subsequent time points, given the previous ones, even when training the model with limited time-point data. Our study demonstrates the potential of the ADPM as a tool for monitoring and forecasting the progression of Alzheimer's disease.

This research introduces a method for understanding natural language through consideration of interactions between words and the broader linguistic context. A novel neural network architecture is proposed, capable of capturing relationships between individual words and the overall semantic meaning of sentences. By leveraging linguistic patterns within specific domains, the network's performance in predicting the meanings of novel sentences can be fine-tuned. Evaluation of this approach occurs through assessment of the network's capacity to identify the dominant semantic element in sentences, and results demonstrate superiority over existing recurrent neural networks. Furthermore, the study presents methods for analyzing and visualizing the network's structural information, enabling the importance of individual words and linguistic patterns to be quantified. Using the system's structural information, the study proposes a method for adapting the network to specific domains, thereby enhancing its performance in predicting the meanings of novel sentences.

Recent breakthroughs in experiments involving artificial matter have sparked an intense interest in understanding how different types of interactions affect the behavior of quantum systems.  A specific model that incorporates all these effects is a quantum system consisting of distinguishable particles with Dirac cones and where each particle affects the others through various interactions.  Previous research found that when these interactions are present, they disrupt the behavior of the system in a way that depends on its momentum, limiting its ability to be described using a simple effective model.  However, a new effective model is proposed, taking into consideration how interactions affect how positions and properties intermingle, leading to an augmentation of the system's Dirac cones.  By applying a simple model that accounts for how interactions affect the system's energy levels, it's shown that these properties can be recovered and in fact predict a notable change in how the system's energy levels change with momentum.  A notable consequence of this is that, without any actual changes to the system's underlying properties, it's possible to observe large, measurable changes in various physical properties such as the system's density of states and its capacity to conduct electricity, specifically in a way that conforms to experimentally observable patterns.

In certain theories involving dark matter, it's suggested that dark matter particles undergo a significant event, known as phase transitions, where they transition from a initial state to a final state. A proposed shadow matter theory suggests that dark matter particles initially resemble particles with a high number of copies, but this transition leads to a deconstruction of these copies, leaving behind a final state that resembles cold dark matter.  Through the use of effective field theory, it's been shown that if dark matter particles initially had a significant event, known as a phase transition, this transition would likely leave behind characteristic signals, known as gravitational waves, that can be detected.  A proposed framework, known as the Metastable Conformal Shadow Matter framework, is shown to be a model that fits these predictions, allowing for a in-depth analysis of this transition, while also aligning with certain constraints, known as cosmic microwave background and large scale structure observations.

Conformal prediction is a powerful supervised learning technique that enables accurate assessment of uncertainty in machine learning models, particularly those used in medical device development. As more AI-based medical devices reach the market, it is crucial for their efficacy to be re-evaluated based on real-world data, presenting a challenge known as distribution shift. Where traditional models often fail, conformal prediction has shown promise in addressing this issue by providing accurate predictions and uncertainty estimates even when there is a change in the data distribution. In this study, we examine the performance of a conformal prediction approach called the maxima swap method when applied to binary classification medical devices subject to various types of distribution shift. We evaluate the efficacy of these devices under 28 distinct scenarios, comparing it to a calibrated Bayesian model and showing that the uncalibrated maxima swap method surpasses the calibrated Bayesian approach in estimating classification labels and uncertainty.

High-fidelity simulations involving chemical processes of DNA, either as a double-stranded entity or in individual nucleic acids, reveal crucial details about their behavior. Specifically, two notable techniques, the force-probing approach (for double-stranded DNA) and the indenter-DNA (for individual nucleotides), utilize an immobile substrate to probe DNA mechanics and also facilitate the investigation of nucleotide association. In this research, we examine the relationship between these methods and explore their potential in analyzing distinct DNA configurations through an enhanced sampling technique, involving Brownian dynamics on a fixed structure. Moreover, these strategies open up possibilities for exploring DNA's capacity to withstand external forces, such as mechanical stress and the effects of ligands, while maintaining accuracy in representing DNA mechanics.

As advancements are made to achieve better stability and stability characteristics in analog-to-digital converter (ADC) design, researchers have been delving into the analog noise sensitivity (ANS) metric, which evaluates an ADC's performance under uncertain conditions. This paper explains why an entropy based approach to assess ANS is more reliable than other methods and presents a new model for non-linear analog noise sensitivity (NLANS). This refinement bridges the gap between existing models and an entropy based approach. Analytical examination and simulations show that NLANS captures the essence of an ADC's resilience in the presence of disturbances better than other models. This better alignment is demonstrated through more accurate relationships between ANS metrics and performance metrics, such as estimation error.

The dielectric characteristics of the pore solution in cement-based materials directly relate to the overall dielectric behavior of the materials. To determine how fluid chemistry affects dielectric spectra, we measured the dielectric constants of aqueous solutions containing various concentrations of calcium hydroxide, calcium chloride, and silicate ions. Our findings reveal that an increase in ionic strength leads to the portlandite solubility equilibrium's convergence and the system's simplified behavior from a standpoint of dielectric theory. Utilizing the parameters obtained, we created a model to explain portlandite coexistence with the pore solution and the observed results. This approach may also be applied to the analysis of other cement-based materials containing supplementary cementitious materials.

In a two-fold scenario where heavy hadrons are treated as non-relativistic bound states composed of other heavy hadrons, this research explores the fundamental properties of these composite objects. Utilizing recent discoveries as a benchmark, our predictions for particles such as $Y(4260)$, $Y(4274)$, and $Y(4365)$ as molecular entities in their own right are validated. Furthermore, we generate an updated model of the $X(4140)$ as a $JS$ state, and our predictions for the $T_{cc}$(4020)$\to D^0\bar{D}^0 J/\psi$ transition width are consistent with the LHCb experiment's observed results. Additionally, in a three-body decay scenario, our predictions for the $T_{cc}$(4020)$\to D^0\bar{D}^0 J/\psi$ decay rate based on a $T_{cc}$(3930)$\to T_{cc}$(3422)$\bar{T}_{cc}$(2309)$ cross-section of about $0.2\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$ are presented. As for the $\chi_{c1,3}(3872)\to D^0\bar{D}^0\gamma$ decay, our predictions for the $T_{cc}$(4020)$\to D^0\bar{D}^0 J/\psi$ decay rate

Research on military unmanned systems is growing as these systems demonstrate the ability to complete tasks more safely and efficiently. However, specific domain-related challenges unique to warfare need to be addressed in developing practical technologies. The application of Natural Language Processing in unmanned systems research is intriguing, as it enables the analysis of underlying trends in scientific publications to identify areas that require further attention. A study has been conducted to examine the development trajectory in military unmanned systems by leveraging NLP and computing tools to process vast amounts of scientific literature. The analysis focuses on the most prominent co-citations in relevant journals and magazines, revealing prominent research drivers. The study reveals that current unmanned systems advancements are heavily influenced by various fields such as mathematics, physics, engineering, and medicine, with evident links to surveillance, communication, information processing, and medical treatment. The findings also highlight major technological and operational areas that warrant continued exploration.

Recent large-scale simulations have found that the characteristics of cold dark matter remain a mystery and have a significant impact on our comprehension of the cosmological data. To clarify the cosmological data, we have used the mock Lyman-$\alpha$ forest simulations to investigate the properties of the cosmological transmission, specifically its cross-correlation with fluorescent light emitted by post-bion absorption lines. These simulations enabled us to identify the key factors influencing the transmission-corrected cross-correlation, allowing for an objective selection of the optimal parameters. Notably, we selected a set of parameters that optimize the transmission-corrected cross-correlation and are consistent with the observed data from two sources, making it possible to obtain direct cosmological deductions. Additionally, we calculated the redshift drift, the distance to first magnetics effect, and the baryon oscillation scale based on the properties of the cross-correlation, producing the following results: the cosmological matter density is approximately $0.317$, the cosmological dark matter density is approximately $0.326$, the cosmological density of neutral hydrogen is approximately $0.546$ and the cosmological index for the coupling between dark matter and a hypothetical particle has a lower limit of approximately $-0.35$. These findings agree with the results from the Planck satellite data and the results of other independent research, specifically CMB, LSS, and BAO data as well as recent data from the spectrum of primordial fluctuations.

Researchers at Fermilab have successfully conducted an experiment where a beam of particles is intentionally manipulated to change its direction using a magnetic field, resulting in the transfer of its horizontal and longitudinal movement patterns. The experiment demonstrated a reduced beam size of approximately 67% in the horizontal axis and a spread out beam size of around 3.6% in the longitudinal axis. The probability of this occurrence was estimated to be around 83%, and the results were obtained using a simulation based on the theory of particle motion. The experiment was carried out using a beam of protons with an initial energy of 120 GeV, and the results were obtained from the A0 beamline. The accuracy of the results was verified by comparing them to a simulation of the beam line, and the expected changes in beam size were confirmed. The experiment was completed in 2019 and used a beam with an initial convergence of around 0.4 GeV/km.

A crucial capability for autonomous vehicles and robotic navigation systems is predicting future trajectories of other road users. Current approaches often neglect the dynamic nature of road user movements and the influence of social awareness, making them inadequate for practical application. This research presents a novel trajectory prediction method built on the principles of cyclic variational autoencoders. The model consists of a sliding sequential CVAE and a socially-aware reevaluation module that utilizes road user interactions to refine predicted trajectories. By integrating these modules, the model generates accurate predictions of each road user's future trajectory while considering the interactions of all road users. Our method was evaluated using the Interaction Bowl dataset and compared to baseline approaches, demonstrating superior performance with higher multi-objective scores.

The concept of information complexity in Boltzmann Machines has garnered attention in past research, with some studies suggesting its potential superiority over circuit complexity. Our study aims to compare different measures of complexity captured through information-theoretic metrics, such as conditional entropy, mutual information, and total correlation, on selected BM circuits. By examining the variability of these measures over multiple runs of the same model, and analyzing their linear correlations, we hope to establish which measures are highly dependent on specific conditions and may provide distinct insights into the complexity of BM systems.

The integration of humans and swarms of autonomous vehicles holds significant potential for streamlined and efficient interaction.  As a result, there is a growing need to develop convenient and automatic methods for data exchange between humans and swarms, particularly through hand gesture recognition, given the inherent adaptability and ease of interpretation for visual-based signals.  This research focuses on identifying a minimal and universally applicable set of hand signals to enable straightforward, efficient, and automatic communication between swarms and humans, paving the way for seamless, real-time control of the swarm by a human operator, utilizing autoencoder-based feature extraction for distinct gesture categories.

The study aims to improve the accuracy of a pioneering deep neural network model developed for identifying five distinct types of human blood cells, which has a high overall accuracy of 95.8%. To increase its accuracy, the model's classification outputs were combined with the predictions generated by three, previously trained neural network models designed for individual cell types. The model's performance was evaluated using a range of metrics, including precision, recall, and the F1-measure, from the classification output. The resulting combined system was then used to classify an unseen dataset of blood cell images, which is referred to as the test dataset. The system achieved an increased overall accuracy of 97.6%, as well as improved precision and recall for individual cell types when compared to the original model.

A new method of controlled quantum dynamics, called the variational counterdiabatic driving technique, minimizes the duration and increases the robustness of quantum state transitions. It has been successfully applied to a model where our developed method outperforms conventional approaches, particularly in a situation where materials with opposing electronic properties are simulated. When initializing the ground state of a complex set of interconnected Hubbard particles, our method demonstrates superior performance, in contrast to the traditional quantum state preparation methods. Not only does it result in a more reliable procedure, but it also reduces the overall timeframe and amplifies the resilience of the driving protocol. Through numerical simulations, we have verified the effectiveness of our method.

This work introduces an efficient image colorization method tailored for tone mapping applications, achieving rapid processing times of over 30 frames per second (fps) on standard hardware. The proposed algorithm employs a time-efficient approach to determine optimal color temperatures for image colors, then calibrates each channel of the LUT accordingly. Experimental results on various images demonstrate the efficacy of the method, which outperforms alternative high-speed solutions in terms of image quality. The accompanying video demonstrates the method's dynamic effect when applied to a sequence of images in real-time. Additionally, the provided LUT files enable effortless use of the proposed method in any tone mapping application, including live real-time processing. The empirical code and resources are publicly available on GitHub.

This research presents an innovative method for expanding series of exponential functions into informative, data-driven polynomial forms that capture essential aspects of the original exponential. Focusing on the initial behavior of these expansions, our analysis demonstrates that under specified conditions, this expansion will converge upon the original exponential, providing a configuration for its approximation. Notably, this polynomial representation retains key attributes of the exponential, including positive definiteness and strict positive definiteness, ensuring it seamlessly adapts to various applications, including the construction of stable probabilistic models. Importantly, this expansion can be employed for functions of multiple variables and is remarkably versatile, applicable to diverse exponential functions defined by specific matrices.

Given a surface S equipped with a metric d, such that it meets the conditions set by Alexandrov for an upper curvature bound, we demonstrate that an almost conformal harmonic map from S to a space M, which is also bounded below by a constant, can be topologically embedded within a space consisting of the mappings from S to M that preserve the metric's features. Consequently, elicitating whether an almost conformal harmonic map is indeed conformal, has significant implications for understanding the behavior of harmonic maps. In the context of n-dimensional space, it has been observed that an almost conformal harmonic map can actually be conformal, given the presence of a universal conformal reparameterization. Additionally, in the case of a surface S, it has been shown that an almost conformal map to a space M is embedded within a space consisting of the group's features, a fact which was previously noted by the authors. As a result of this, it has been proven that any surface S, which features a metric induced by an Alexandrov curvature d, can be normalized to conform to a space consisting of the features of M, a phenomenon also known as uniformization.

A novel approach has been developed for investigating photon-photon interactions
using a laser-plasma platform. This setup yields a range of physical phenomena
inspired by quantum field theory, specifically processes such as particle creation
and scattering, taking place within plasma waves. To date, the limitations of existing
technologies have made it challenging to observe double Compton scattering, a key
predictive interaction in quantum field theory. Our laser-plasma framework provides
a new route for investigating this phenomenon, offering a theoretical model along with
predicted outcomes for an experiment set to take place at the National Ignition Facility
(NIF) at the Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL).

In a 2HDM framework where $Z_2$ is broken with a non-zero mass, $m_{12}$, with a very large ratio of $v_1/v_2$, two characteristics arise. When $m_{12}$ is small, a specific mechanism generates a light, pseudo-scalar particle that can influence the mass of $h$ through a loop effect (the $h\to aa$ process). However, as $m_{12}$ increases, this effect diminishes, and a new, standard process $h\to a_a$ becomes prominent. However, this process is restricted by constraints on the cross-sectional process $pp\to Za\to Za$, particularly when $Z$ bosons are produced at the very forward angle of about $10^{-5}$. For $h$ decays, its branching ratio to $a$ is limited to about $0.10$. Furthermore, as $m_{12}$ increases beyond $1500$ $\mathrm{GeV}^2$, the predicted mass of $a$ begins to differ significantly from its standard model equivalent by about $20\,\mathrm{GeV}$.

The RDF data model provides an unstructured format that is typically used for query, inference, and integration purposes, but it lacks organization, making it unsuitable for services and applications until additional constraints are applied. Various approaches have been employed to add structure and order to RDF data, with some solutions relying on XML schema, global database schemas, or constraints defined using rule languages. A recent addition, Shape Expression (SHEX), enables specifying constraints and operations for RDF data, but its primary focus is on data quality rather than enabling tasks such as query, caching, or mapping that require full structural representation. To bridge this gap, our work introduces a comprehensive mapping from constrained RDF data, defined using SHEX, to its corresponding RDF Triples, effectively enabling an orderly representation of data. This allows for tasks like query preparation, caching, or mapping, in domains where SHEX constraints apply, to be based on the triple representation of the data. To achieve this mapping, we employ SHEX constraints and RDF views, combining them with the existing SHEX validation process to ensure the resulting views are always valid with respect to the original data.

A topic of great interest in fields such as economics, technology policy, and communication science has been the topic of frontier estimation. This paper provides an open-source Python extension for the popular R package StoNED, widely regarded as the most advanced and robust tool for frontier estimation to date. The extended PyStoNED package incorporates new functionality, including the capacity to handle complex data structures featuring multiple output variables and intricate index systems. In addition, PyStoNED offers improved tools for data exploration, such as graphical visualizations and data summary reports. The extension also includes options for performing standard and non-parametric frontier estimations, creating new data frames with the estimated outputs, and generating key metrics including the number of efficient units, their overall efficiency, and a range of alternative efficiency measures. To highlight the capabilities of PyStoNED, we use it to analyze a dataset of 281 banks from the Baltics, estimating and analyzing the technical, scale, and technical pure efficiencies of banks over a four-year period.

In a scenario where supersymmetry is absent, our research explores the behavior of two heavy top-quark pairs in association with a neutral Higgs boson within the standard model of particle physics. We identify the optimal strategy for detecting the 125 GeV Higgs boson with the highest priority and then determine the sensitivity of the 13 TeV Large Hadron Collider to this process and its outcome across various energy configurations. A significant finding indicates that the PPP process can detect the 125 Higgs boson at a 99.5% confidence level when assuming the standard model's predictions and accounting for a luminosity of 300 inverse femtobarns. Additionally, the study examines the standard model's predictions for the 126 GeV doublet Higgs bosons in this same production mechanism. It has been found that the 306 GeV charged Higgs boson can be detected at the 99.5% confidence level when assuming the standard model's predictions and accounting for a luminosity of 300 inverse femtobarns. Similarly, the 125 GeV and 126 GeV neutral Higgs bosons can be detected at the same confidence level when their production branching ratios meet specific criteria.

Recent advancements in natural language processing have seen significant improvements, primarily driven by large-scale language model training. To address complex tasks in multiple domains, these models are often fine-tuned on small datasets. However, the traditional approach to task-specific training can be inefficient, as it typically requires extensive task-explanation and expensive dataset acquisition. This paper argues that these steps should be reduced or eliminated if possible. Based on this idea, we develop an unsupervised technique for domain discovery and adaptation from a pre-trained language model without exhaustive task-explanation and dataset acquisition. Moreover, we propose a pioneering few-shot learning algorithm that gradually builds a model's capacity to perform tasks as it receives a limited number of examples. We test these innovations against other prominent methods on datasets for argumentative and non-argumentative text generation in multiple domains, with our results indicating substantial performance gains. Notably, our model consistently achieves data-driven results superior to the benchmark solution, often by a significant margin.

The precision of automated speech recognition systems has improved significantly in recent years, especially for English. Nonetheless, accurately translating German speech remains a persisting challenge. In this study, we assessed the performance of three established speech recognition systems - Kaldi, FFmpegKaldi, and MuMa - on German dialogue data. While the systems achieved a respectable 89.6% to 89.7% correct word recognition rate, they failed to meet our standards for practical application in a community project. Subsequently, we developed a new system, named SchwarzeOeffner, incorporating essential elements from all three models and leveraging an expansive German corpus recorded under high-quality conditions, thereby significantly enhancing accuracy.

An investigation of Be-type stars within the 30 Doradus star cluster of the Large Magellanic Cloud has revealed some intriguing findings. Observations spanning the spectral range from ultraviolet to near infrared were collected and used to determine the properties of the Be-type stars, along with the orbital parameters for two binary systems. Notably, our results show that the luminosities of the Be-type stars in 30 Doradus tend to be lower than expected, and this may be due to the effects of significant line losses, particularly in the ultraviolet spectrum. Furthermore, our study suggests that the Be-type stars within 30 Doradus are often accompanied by compact radio sources, and this may be related to the presence of a disk populated by electron orbits.

To translate automated speech recognition output into standard written language, we develop a data-driven model for inverse text normalization. This model is trained on pairs of written text and normalized speech recognition output. However, the quality of speech recognition output limits its effectiveness. In particular, the model struggles with speech data that features filler words like "you know" and data silencing represented by an underscore. By incorporating data augmentation techniques that fill silences with filler words and enhance speech generation with knowledge of the language structure, our proposed model outperforms previous solutions. This study presents a groundbreaking method for producing groundbreaking text generation techniques, specifically a context-based filler-filled filling model and an underscore-based filler replacement model. In experiments, our proposed model outperformed baseline models.

This paper demonstrates a Faber-Krahn type inequality for the first eigenvalue 
of the Hermite operator when subject to Robin boundary conditions, showing 
that the optimal configuration is a half-space, and investigates the conditions 
under which equality occurs.

Tangent kernel methods build efficient and lightweight representations of complex data by leveraging low-level patterns inherent to the data's underlying distribution. We develop a novel family of tangent kernel classifiers and regressors by integrating various distribution modes, including a more flexible non-exchangeable mechanism, into a unified framework. Our generic construction methodology allows for the incorporation of additional trainable parameters, enabling improved flexibility and contaminated distribution learning. Empirically, our proposed algorithms outperform previous tangent kernel solutions in various settings, especially on more challenging non-linear tasks.

We examine the non-Hermitian point-gap topology of one-dimensional non-Hermitian Hamiltonians when subject to correlations in disorder. For the diagonal disorder model, we find that correlations in disorder lead to a reduced point-gap topology, with exceptional points replaced by point-Garrod points, possessing the same geometric winding numbers as before. For the off-diagonal disorder model, we obtain an analogous outcome, with correlations in disorder preserving the point-Garrod point spectrum while restructuring the gap's geometric winding numbers. These findings enable the construction of visions for the extended non-Hermitian point-gap topology in one-dimensional systems and suggest potential applications in quantum emitters. Furthermore, to visually represent the extended non-Hermitian point-gap topology, we developed a geometric mapping of one-dimensional non-Hermitian Hamiltonians onto a two-dimensional complex plane, with corresponding observations from two studies on non-Hermitian band touchings and the extended non-Hermitian point-gap topology serving as a foundation.

Our research focuses on the characteristics that define a speaker's individuality in spoken language. We evaluate a learning-based approach that allows a neural network to capture these characteristics from recorded speech and generate a similar identity in synthetic speech. Our study investigates the impact of two key factors on incorporating these characteristics into synthetic speech: the speaker's own recorded speech and the identification of distinct identities. We examine this approach through both perceived speaker identity and emotional expression in spoken language.
